predecessors.name: Portuguese Empire
predecessors.text: the Kingdom of Brazil and the Cisplatina province of the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves, with Portuguese garrisons still at Salvador, São Luís, Belém and Montevideo in 1822

successors.name: Brazilian Republic
successors.text: the whole country, after the coup of 15 November 1889 'instituted the republic'

ledger.x: 7 September 1822: Pedro declares Brazil independent.
1822: the Portuguese hold Salvador.
1822: Maranhão and Pará stay loyal to Portugal.
1822: the Portuguese regiments in Montevideo.
1823: Maranhão and Pará fall in line.
2 July 1823: Salvador surrenders.
Beginning of 1824: the Portuguese leave Montevideo.
2 July 1824: Pernambuco rebels proclaim the Confederation of the Equator.
September 1824: the Confederation of the Equator is crushed.
19 April 1825: the Thirty-Three Orientals land.
ledger.cpn: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

ledger.x: 27 August 1828: the Preliminary Peace Convention.
ledger.cpn: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

ledger.x: 27 August 1828: Cisplatina becomes independent as Uruguay.
6-7 January 1835: the Cabanagem rebels take Belém.
20 September 1835: the Ragamuffin revolt begins.
11 September 1836: the Riograndense Republic is proclaimed.
1839: the rebels proclaim the Juliana Republic in Santa Catarina 'following the capture of Laguna'; it 'fell back into imperial hands after four months'.
1839: Laguna returns to the empire after four months; the Juliana Republic is gone.
1840: the last Cabanagem rebels yield.
1 March 1845: the Treaty of Ponche Verde ends the Ragamuffin War.
1 March 1845: Rio Grande do Sul returns to the Empire.
1853: the north-west Amazon enters Cliopatria's outline.
14 December 1864: Paraguay invades Mato Grosso and holds the southern districts.
12 June 1865: the Paraguayans take São Borja and hold the Uruguay river towns.
18 September 1865: Uruguaiana surrenders and the occupation of Rio Grande do Sul ends.
27 March 1867: the Treaty of Ayacucho with Bolivia.
Bridged to the same treaty of 27 March 1867.
1868: Paraguay withdraws from Mato Grosso.
25 July 1868: Humaitá falls and the Allies overrun Paraguay.
9 January 1872: the Loizaga-Cotegipe Treaty.
1876: the Allied occupation of Paraguay ends.
1877: 40 cells of Roraima enter the outline, held by no Cliopatria shape in 1870.
15 November 1889: the republican coup ends the Empire.

wars.name: Brazilian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Independentist victory: Salvador surrendered on 2 July 1823, Cochrane secured Maranhão and Pará, the Royal Volunteers left Cisplatina at the beginning of 1824; the Treaty of Rio de Janeiro (29 August 1825, in force 15 November 1825) ended the war.

wars.name: Confederation of the Equator
wars.outcome: Proclaimed on 2 July 1824; Olinda and a few villages of southern Ceará and Paraíba; the army attacked Recife on 12 September and the rebels were defeated five days later.

wars.name: Cisplatine War
wars.outcome: Brazil declared war on 10 December 1825 (infobox 10 December 1825 - 27 August 1828); there was fighting at Sarandí (12 October 1825) and Ituzaingó/Passo do Rosário (20 February 1827), the Argentines defeated the Brazilian flotilla at Juncal, and Brazil…

wars.name: Cabanagem
wars.outcome: The rebels took Belém on 6 January 1835, left it in April 1836 and resisted in the interior until the last group yielded in 1840; more than 40,000 dead.

wars.name: Ragamuffin War
wars.outcome: The Riograndense Republic was proclaimed on 11 September 1836; the Juliana Republic of 1839 lasted four months; the Treaty of Ponche Verde of 1 March 1845 reintegrated both.

wars.name: Paraguayan War
wars.outcome: Paraguay invaded Mato Grosso (14 December 1864) and Rio Grande do Sul (June 1865); the Allies invaded Paraguay on 16 April 1866, took Humaitá on 25 July 1868 and Asunción on 1 January 1869; López died at Cerro Corá on 1 March 1870; the Loizaga-Cotegipe Treaty…

certainty.note: No treaty fixes the Amazon, Mato Grosso or Missions frontiers; the Cisplatina limit is a war line to 1828.

Treaty lines exist with Uruguay (1851), Peru (1851 and 1874), Bolivia (27 March 1867) and Paraguay (9 January 1872), but 'demarcation of the borders was not started until the end of the 19th century' and the Amazon frontier is approximate…
